topic: Diagnostic Support Filtering and Latent Factor Utility Evidence
problem_statement: Provide empirical evidence on whether ALS latent factor representations contain genuine user preference signal or whether 0 HitRate is due to complete representation failure.
root_cause: Fluke bias crowds Top-N recommendation slots with uninformative 1-rating items, making it impossible to observe latent factor ranking utility.
solution_or_decision: Execute controlled diagnostic branch ALS_PLUS_TRAIN_SUPPORT_FILTER using the same learned factor vectors but masking low-support items (< 5 ratings and < 20 ratings). Kept strictly separated from ALS_ONLY model family to maintain scientific integrity.
evidence: Masking items with < 5 ratings drops 1-rating slots to 0.00% and elevates >100 ratings slots to 15.91%. Masking items with < 20 ratings elevates >100 ratings slots to 76.04% and yields positive Screening HR@10 = 0.00022 and NDCG@10 = 0.00010 (1 hit), proving latent factors carry genuine ranking signal when fluke noise is removed.
